--- /dev/null
+++ b/services/preferences/scripts/backfill-v2.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+// Copies every item from the v1 table (customerId key) into the v2 table
+// (accountId + customerId key); v1 items already carry accountId as a plain
+// attribute. Run once per stage after the stack update:
+//   OLD_TABLE=<v1 physical name> NEW_TABLE=<v2 physical name> npx tsx scripts/backfill-v2.ts
+import { DynamoDBClient } from "@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb";
+import { DynamoDBDocumentClient, ScanCommand, BatchWriteCommand } from "@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb";
+
+const oldTable = process.env.OLD_TABLE;
+const newTable = process.env.NEW_TABLE;
+if (!oldTable || !newTable) {
+  throw new Error("OLD_TABLE and NEW_TABLE are required");
+}
+
+const db = DynamoDBDocumentClient.from(new DynamoDBClient({}));
+
+async function main(): Promise<void> {
+  let startKey: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
+  let copied = 0;
+  do {
+    const page = await db.send(new ScanCommand({ TableName: oldTable, ExclusiveStartKey: startKey }));
+    const items = page.Items ?? [];
+    for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i += 25) {
+      const batch = items.slice(i, i + 25).map((item) => ({
+        PutRequest: { Item: item },
+      }));
+      const res = await db.send(new BatchWriteCommand({ RequestItems: { [newTable]: batch } }));
+      if (res.UnprocessedItems && Object.keys(res.UnprocessedItems).length > 0) {
+        throw new Error(`unprocessed items after copying ${copied}`);
+      }
+      copied += batch.length;
+    }
+    startKey = page.LastEvaluatedKey;
+  } while (startKey);
+  console.log(`copied ${copied} items from ${oldTable} to ${newTable}`);
+}
+
+main().catch((err) => {
+  console.error(err);
+  process.exit(1);
+});

cases.planted: services/preferences/template.yaml changes the KeySchema and attribute definitions of `PreferencesTable`, an update that requires replacement, and adds `DeletionPolicy: Retain` as the safeguard. DeletionPolicy applies when a resource is removed from the stack or the stack is deleted, not on replacement: CloudFormation creates the new table, repoints every `!Ref` to it, then deletes the old one under UpdateReplacePolicy, which defaults to Delete. The stack update therefore deletes the v1 table with every customer's preferences before `scripts/backfill-v2.ts` can copy from it. `UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain`, or a new table under a new logical id, is what keeps the old table.

cases.summary: Extract the orders table and its alarm into an OrdersData construct
cases.planted: infra/lib/orders-stack.ts now creates the table inside `new OrdersData(this, 'Data', ...)`, and lib/constructs/orders-data.ts keeps the child id `OrdersTable`, so the table's construct path changes from OrdersTable to Data/OrdersTable. CDK derives the CloudFormation logical id from that path, so the next deploy sees one resource removed and a new one added: it creates a new, empty table, points TABLE_NAME and the grants at it, and drops the old table from the stack (kept by the default RETAIN policy, but orphaned). From that deploy on, production orders are read and written against an empty table. Keeping the logical id (a `Default` child id, `cdk refactor`, or an override) avoids the replacement.

 import type { FastifyInstance } from "fastify";
 import { pool } from "./db";
+import { EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION } from "./schema-version";
 
 export function registerHealth(app: FastifyInstance): void {
   app.get("/livez", async () => ({ status: "ok" }));

In the unchanged deploy workflow the migrations run in the step after `helm upgrade --wait`, which waits for the new pods to become ready. On every release that adds a migration the new pods stay unready because the schema is behind, Helm times out after 10 minutes and the job fails, and the migration step after it never runs, so the schema never catches up and such a release can never ship.
